=== Overview ===
From the settlement of Ōaza Fushihara (ふしはら), if one climbs to the end of Dō no Tani (Hall Valley), the shrine is enshrined facing south on a {{ill|Hügelland|cs|Pahorkatina|de|Hügelland|fr|Basse montagne|hak|Khiu-lîn|ja|丘陵|ko|구릉|nl|Heuvelland (landschap)|pl|Wysoczyzna|sk|Pahorkatina|zh|丘陵|zh_classical|丘陵|zh_yue|丘陵|qid=Q222912}} on the right side near the summit.

It is an ancient shrine also mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}, but the origins and history of its founding are not clear.

However, there is a theory that, based on its location along a valley behind the village, it was enshrined as a deity protecting agricultural water.

The {{ill|Saijin|abstract|Q11591100|fr|Saijin|ja|祭神|zh|祭神|qid=Q11591100}} is {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame no Koyane}}.

However, in the Nihon Sōkoku Fudoki, the name {{ill|Toyotama-hime|de|Toyotama-hime|es|Toyotama-hime|fa|تویوتاما-هیمه|fi|Otohime|fr|Otohime|id|Toyotama-hime|ja|トヨタマヒメ|ko|도요타마히메|mni|ꯇꯣꯌꯣꯇꯃ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Toyotama-hime|ru|Тоётама-химэ|simple|Toyotama-hime|sv|Otohime|uk|Тойотама-хіме|vi|Toyotama-hime|zh|豐玉毘賣命|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime}} appears, and in the {{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092|lt=Tokusen Shinmyōchō}}, the name {{ill|Tamakushi-hime|Q11572681|qid=Q11572681|lt=Tamakushihime}} appears, suggesting that the principal deity changed during the medieval period.

The auxiliary shrine on the right side of the grounds is dedicated to {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|Q91088537|qid=Q91088537|lt=Ame no Oshikumone no Mikoto}}<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=平群町史|publisher=平群町役場|pages=665-667}}</ref>.

The auxiliary shrine outside the tamagaki (sacred fence) of the main hall is recorded in the {{ill|jinjameisaichou|Q11590704|qid=Q11590704}} as "enshrined deity unknown, or possibly Ōnamuji no Mikoto."

The Hachiōji Shrine on the hill to the left has a natural stone as its sacred object, and the same Meisaichō records it as "enshrined deity unknown, or possibly Yahashira no Kami"<ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=平群町史編集委員会|title=平群町史|publisher=平群町役場|date=1976-04|ncid=BN04492478|pages=665-667}}</ref>.

On the hamayuka (floor platform) in front of the main hall doors, there are clay komainu (guardian dogs), which are rare in this area.
